intro.title: useWindowSize
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useWindowSize` that tracks and returns the current width and height of the browser window. You'll learn how to use the `useState` and `useEffect` hooks to manage state and handle side effects, such as listening to the browser's `resize` event. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the browser's native `window` object. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that automatically updates your component whenever the window size changes.
intro.usecase: The useWindowSize hook is essential for creating responsive layouts that adapt to different screen sizes in real-world applications. In e-commerce sites, product grids automatically rearrange from multi-column layouts on desktops to single-column views on mobile devices. Dashboard applications use window size detection to show/hide side panels or adjust chart dimensions when users resize their browser windows. Media players and video conferencing tools rely on window size to optimize video quality and UI element placement for the available screen space.
